_comment: Threat-projection field, consumer 1 (owner-originated design, 2026-07-09; docs/THREAT_LAYER_PROPOSAL.md), env-gated SWEG_THREAT_CHARGE, default OFF, byte-identical when unset. This is an ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE PILOTING HEURISTIC, NOT a Warhammer 40,000 10th-edition game rule — there is no codex or core rule that tells a player which enemy to charge. Following the precedent of simulator.target_economics, simulator.focus_fire and simulator.persistent_nomination (all explicitly-flagged AI design heuristics), this entry quotes the core wound-roll-and-save wording the field's expected-wounds math is built from, and cites the real-play 'threat range' concept that motivates it: a competent player prices a destination against the incoming damage every enemy can project onto it next turn (its guns at range plus its move-and-charge melee reach with a probability gradient), and understands that killing the charge target removes that target's contribution from the field. THE GAP this consumer addresses: the legacy charge picker (strategy.py pick_charge_target) reads ONLY the target's own melee output back at the charger — score = value / (1 + threat_against_target) — so a unit charging one of two adjacent Khorne Berzerker squads is blind to the second squad's counter-charge and to any gunline that will delete it in the open next turn. The mechanic does not change combat math or draw any new random number — it only re-points the picker's argmax among already-legal in-range charge candidates toward destinations whose realized post-fight incoming threat the charger can afford.

simulator.threat_projection_charge.rule_name: Wound roll (Strength vs Toughness) + Saving throw / invulnerable save + Charge roll (2D6) (10e Core Rules) — charge-target-priority piloting heuristic
simulator.threat_projection_charge.quoted_text: If the Strength characteristic of the weapon used is equal to the Toughness characteristic of the target model's unit, a Wound roll of 4+ is required... for each of those attacks that successfully wounded the target unit, the player commanding that unit can attempt a saving throw... if that unit has an invulnerable save, the player can use that instead of their normal saving throw... To make a charge roll, roll 2D6. The unit can make a Charge move if the result is greater than or equal to the distance (in inches) between it and the closest enemy unit it wishes to charge.
simulator.threat_projection_charge.trigger: SWEG_THREAT_CHARGE=1 (default off, byte-identical when unset). In strategy.py pick_charge_target, for the charge destination of each candidate target, build the incoming threat field T at that cell over every LIVING enemy E: threat_E = ranged_expected_wounds(E -> charger) (reusing simulator._ranged_expected_wounds — shots, hit fraction, Strength-vs-Toughness wound fraction raised to any matching Anti-X floor, the unsaved fraction after armour or invulnerable save, damage per shot) when the cell is within E's Move + weapon range, attenuated by the positional Benefit of Cover at the cell (reusing units.save_probability's +1-save-pip cover math with the 10e INFANTRY 'cannot better 3+ vs AP0' cap); plus melee_expected_wounds(E -> charger) (reusing strategy._kill_potential_wounds) multiplied by P_reach, the exact 2D6 probability E covers the remaining distance after its Move. T_post subtracts the target's own contribution weighted by P(kill), derived from the charger's kill-potential expected wounds against the target's current health.
simulator.threat_projection_charge.effect: AI charge-target-selection heuristic. The picker's per-candidate denominator 1 + threat_against_target (the target's melee output only) is replaced by 1 + T_post/effective_wounds(charger), the post-fight threat FIELD at the charge destination normalised by the charger's remaining wounds (the reused expected-wounds helpers already fold in the charger's save and toughness, so the ratio reads as the fraction of the charger's remaining value forfeited by standing there — a derived, knob-free tolerance). A destination the charger can reach where a SECOND enemy melee squad also has charge reach, or where a gunline still bears, now scores lower than an equally-valuable but isolated target (the two-Berzerker case, priced exactly); a charge that reliably kills its target removes that target's own contribution from the field (T_post = T - threat_target * P(kill)), so deleting an isolated threat stays cheap. Every existing bonus multiplier (gunline / support / screen / synapse / faction tarpit / knight-melee / won't-crack / displacement) is preserved unchanged; the OFF path leaves the legacy denominator byte-identical. This is an AI design heuristic, not a 10e rule — the quoted core wound-roll, saving-throw and 2D6 charge-roll wording is the combat math the field's expected-wounds and reach figures are built from; it does not alter any dice, roll, or damage value, and it draws no new random number. Faithful and even-handed: it fires for ALL factions and prices ANY living enemy's projected threat onto the destination. HONEST CAVEAT (per the proposal): the ranged half is attenuated only by the angle-independent positional cover the sim's shooting RESOLUTION actually enforces, NOT by line-of-sight occlusion — the layer plans with the same geometry the resolution applies; true line-of-sight-blocked planning is deferred to a separate gated rules-fidelity proposal.

_threat_range_doctrine_reference: Real-play doctrine motivating this heuristic, presented as doctrine (not a rules citation) per the same disclosure pattern as the _target_priority_doctrine_reference note in data/rule_citations.d/target_economics.json: competent 10th-edition play evaluates a move or charge against the 'threat range' of every enemy — the sum of an enemy's Movement characteristic and its weapon range (guns) or its Movement plus average 2D6 charge distance (melee) — and prices a destination against the damage that can be projected onto it on the opponent's next turn, declining exposure a unit cannot pay for and committing killy units where the arithmetic says the target dies and stops projecting. Source: https://www.goonhammer.com/how-to-base-your-army-for-competitive-play/ and the broader Goonhammer 'Start Competing' 10th-edition tactics series (already cited elsewhere in this project for the same threat-range / target-priority doctrine), which teach measuring and respecting enemy threat ranges as the core of positional decision-making. NOTE (honesty about verification): consistent with the notes recorded for simulator.target_economics and simulator.focus_fire_completion in this codebase, the Goonhammer pages are JavaScript-rendered and their exact live text could not be re-confirmed by WebFetch this session; the 'threat range' concept paraphrased here is nonetheless the standard real-play tactic the docs/PILOT_FINDINGS.md researched playbooks already cite, and the proposal (docs/THREAT_LAYER_PROPOSAL.md) records it as the mechanism this layer models.
